tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Which mode this connection is in — anonymous (read-only) or a project — and what that unlocks.

tools.name: join_waitlist
tools.description: Put the founder on the marketinque waitlist for a project (the idea queue, kit, dossier, signals, nightly routine — the paid tier, opening soon). Call ONLY after the founder gave you their email and said yes in this session; `confirmed` attests that. One email, no spam; they can unsubscribe from any

tools.name: get_plan
tools.description: The launch plan. With no `node`: the outline — phases and objectives with step counts. With `node` (a phase or objective slug): every step under it, with status and whether it is unlocked. Anonymous callers pass `done`/`not_applicable`/`traits`; a project uses its own.

tools.name: get_step
tools.description: One plan step in full: title, detail, the target URL where it happens, the play it follows, the prerequisite slugs and whether they are met (unlocked), how it verifies (self, evidence URL or an automatic signal), minutes and cost. Read it before working a step that next_steps or get_plan returned; t

tools.name: next_steps
tools.description: The next unlocked, unstarted steps in tree order, and a sprint packed into `minutes`. Anonymous callers pass `done`/`not_applicable` (from marketinque.json) and `traits`; a project uses its own.

tools.name: list_directories
tools.description: Places that give a startup a backlink, one phase at a time in the order that works. Default phase bl-sprint: the 95 free, dofollow, page-scoped, graded rows. Each row carries its submission page (or where to find it) and, for a project, the listing already recorded.

tools.name: get_directory
tools.description: One directory from the index: domain rating, dofollow, price, category, the submission page URL (or where to look for it), account_required (the page redirected to a sign-in when probed — most rows want a sign-in at submit anyway), founder_fills (a form an agent cannot drive), the note from the last

tools.name: get_submission_kit
tools.description: What every directory form asks for, written once. A project returns its product profile and brand dossier plus the state of the five kit steps; anonymous callers get the five steps to draft from the product site.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_step, get_directory · Public sink: join_waitlist, get_directory.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_step, get_directory · Public sink: join_waitlist, get_directory

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
